intended_object: The eventual-range subfunctor of a cofiltered system F : J ⥤ Type. Its object at j is the eventual range ⋂_{f : i ⟶ j} range(F.map f), and its arrows are F's arrows restricted to these subsets. Inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it (sections equivalence, Mittag-Leffler surjectivity).
explanation: Each object is F.eventualRange j, the intersection of the ranges of all arrows into j. Each arrow is F.map f restricted to the eventual ranges; it is well defined because the lemma eventualRange_mapsTo shows that F.map f sends eventual ranges into eventual ranges. The cofiltered-or-empty hypothesis is genuinely needed for that lemma (its proof uses cospan), so the setting is not too narrow. J is an arbitrary category and the values are arbitrary types. This is the standard construction used to prove that the inverse limit of nonempty finite sets is nonempty, and it matches its uses in the library (toEventualRangesSectionsEquiv, surjective_toEventualRanges).
